newsitem.title: TAIWAN: European Bank to issue T$5.5b Taiwan-dollar bonds.
newsitem.headline: European Bank to issue T$5.5b Taiwan-dollar bonds.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development planned to issue T$5.5 billion (US$200 million) worth of Taiwan dollar-denominated bonds, lead underwriter Grand Cathay Securities said on Monday.
The issue was expected to have a seven-year term, a Grand Cathay official said.
But he declined to reveal more details.
"We still have not received notice of approval from the central bank, so we cannot comment on other aspects such as coupon rate or issue date," he said by telephone.
The central bank declined to confirm it was screening the issue, although it had said earlier that the European bank was interested in launching such a issue.
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development would become the third development bank to issue Taiwan-dollar bonds.
The Central American Bank of Economic Integration plans to issue T$6.8 bllion (US$246 million) Taiwan-dollar bonds on May 16.
The Asian Development Bank issued T$2.6 billion (US$100 million) worth of Taiwan-dollar bonds in August 1995, and launched a T$7 billion (US$255 million) issue in December 1996.
Analysts have said the issues reflect a drive by Taiwan's government to encourage international agencies to raise capital in the island's cash-flush money market.
